{"candidate": {"code": "    def redact_keys(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return a shallow copy of *data* with sensitive values redacted.

        BUG_68: only top-level keys are checked.  Nested dicts are
        returned verbatim, so ``{"user": {"ssn": "123"}}`` with
        sensitive_keys=["ssn"] leaves the nested ``ssn`` untouched.
        The function also fails to call
        ``orgops.auditing.write_event("redaction.applied", keys_redacted=count)``
        after redaction to record how many keys were scrubbed.
        """
        def _redact_impl(obj: Any) -> tuple[Any, int]:
            if not isinstance(obj, dict):
                return obj, 0
            result: dict[str, Any] = {}
            count = 0
            for key, value in obj.items():
                if key.lower() in self.sensitive_keys:
                    result[key] = REDACTED_PLACEHOLDER
                    count += 1
                elif isinstance(value, dict):
                    result[key], nested = _redact_impl(value)
                    count += nested
                else:
                    result[key] = value
            return result, count
        
        redacted, count = _redact_impl(data)
        import orgops.auditing
        orgops.auditing.write_event("redaction.applied", keys_redacted=count)
        return redacted", "comments": "Implement recursive redaction of nested dicts and emit audit event with total key count"}, "constraints": [{"id": "bug68_nested_redaction_and_audit", "voltsnip_key": "voltsnip/script30/hard/bug68/scenario_context/v1", "check": "Recursive nested dict redaction AND audit event via orgops.auditing.write_event.", "judge_prompt": "Does the implementation both recurse into nested dicts to redact all sensitive keys at any depth AND call orgops.auditing.write_event("redaction.applied", keys_redacted=count) with the total count of redacted keys?"}]}
